commits.subject: Show streamed agent text in every open conversation
commits.body:
The live bubble was dropped as soon as a conversation held any structured
message, so after an agent's first reply nothing streamed at all. It now
always follows the stage's conversation: assistant text replaces it as it
grows, its completed message supersedes it (shown once, never next to a
stale bubble), and a new or failed attempt clears it so a half message
never lingers as if final. Tool lines are timeline rows of their own and
no longer overwrite the text, and output chunks stay out of the raw
Activity feed, which would otherwise repaint per chunk.

A browser test drives the full console over a fake socket: chunks patch
the bubble in place (no row repaint, no API reads), then the completion,
a failed attempt and a cancellation (LT-5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Stream agent text from every adapter as it is generated
commits.body:
A turn's text used to reach the task only when a whole message completed:
the Claude Agent SDK ran without partial messages, the Codex app-server
path waited for item/completed, and both metered API rails read
res.json(). ACP did stream, but emitted bare deltas that the console
renders as the whole live message, so it showed only the last chunk.

- Claude Agent SDK: request partial messages and emit the main agent's
  growing text block; sub-agent streams stay out of the main bubble.
- Codex app-server: emit item/agentMessage/delta as the growing text.
- ACP: publish the accumulated text instead of each chunk.
- Messages and Responses API rails: request streaming responses and
  rebuild the exact object the non-streaming call returns, so usage,
  tool calls, stop reasons and error classification are unchanged. A
  mid-stream error event is reported with the HTTP status the same
  error carries before a stream starts; a body cut mid-stream is a
  retryable interruption, never a completed turn. Non-SSE responses
  (proxies, stubs) are read as JSON as before.

The completing item still records the message exactly once; an adapter
no longer re-emits text identical to what it just streamed (LT-5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Coalesce live agent output in the turn runtime
commits.body:
Streaming adapters re-emit the growing text of the block being generated.
Publishing every token as an agent.output event would flood the event log
and every open console, so the provider-neutral runtime now publishes the
first chunk at once and then at most one update per 150 ms carrying the
latest text. Pending text is flushed before any activity that must follow
it (the completed message) and at a successful turn end; a failed or
cancelled turn publishes nothing more, so a half message never lands after
the turn stopped. Groundwork for token streaming in every adapter (LT-5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: Ask the workflow for follow-ups only when one can exist
commits.body:
Every running turn queried the workflow's pendingMessages every 1.2 s. A
query on an execution that has left the worker's small cache replays its
whole history, so a long turn cost ~50 replays a minute for nothing. The
API journals each accepted follow-up as a conversation.message event, and
a workflow that appends a message itself mid-turn (a mode switch)
publishes its view, so the activity now reads those journal entries (an
indexed read) and queries only when one appeared: the first pull always
asks (a message may predate the turn), a journaled follow-up keeps asking
for up to 10 s until it comes back (the query can race the workflow task
applying the signal), and a 30 s backstop still delivers writers that
journal nothing (a raw Temporal signal). Adapter polling cadence, and so
delivery latency, is unchanged.

The runtime's own 1 s heartbeat duplicated the activity's keep-alive,
which already spans the provider call; the turn now has one (LT-13).

The two end-to-end tests that signal Temporal directly mid-turn now
journal the message as the API does.

commits.subject: Push worker events to browsers at once and authorize sockets per task
commits.body:
In process-worker mode the activity child commits events to the shared
database, and the primary's relay only found them on its 500 ms poll:
wake() existed but nothing called it. The child now sends a coalesced
worker.events notice over its supervisor channel after each commit, and
the primary wakes the relay, which feeds the bus and the fanout; polling
remains the recovery path for a lost notice.

Each live event also re-verified the socket's token (scoped-token,
session, account-closure and org reads) and, on refusal, re-derived the
human's capabilities, per event per socket. With streamed output that is
several times a second. A socket now decides each task's visibility once
and reuses it until its token expires, capped at 60 s so a revocation or
membership change still reaches a socket that stays open; a failed lookup
is retried rather than cached (LT-15).

commits.subject: Start tasks without waiting for advisory GitHub and wiki work
commits.body:
Two pieces of work sat between a create request and workflow.start
without being able to change whether or how the task starts:

- The GitHub merge preflight only warns, yet its live permission calls
  (per repository, then per routed reviewer, one after another) ran
  before the start. It now runs alongside the rest of creation and the
  start; the created task still carries its warnings and the warning is
  still journaled, and it journals nothing for a creation that was undone.
  The human-route check that can reject a task still runs first.
- Every create and queue re-ensured the project's local wiki repository:
  three or more git processes in the wiki's per-repository lane, which
  can sit behind a remote fetch/publish. Once this gateway has ensured a
  project's wiki (boot does it for every project), a start refreshes it in
  the background; a project not yet ensured still waits for it (LT-16).
